draft.title: Midpoint of an interval
card: An interval is the part of a line between two end points. Its midpoint is the point exactly halfway between them.
To find the midpoint, average the x-values of the end points. Then average the y-values. To average two numbers, add them and divide by 2.
For end points (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂), the midpoint is ((x₁ + x₂) ÷ 2, (y₁ + y₂) ÷ 2).
Example: the end points are (2, 5) and (8, −1). x: (2 + 8) ÷ 2 = 5. y: (5 + −1) ÷ 2 = 2. The midpoint is (5, 2).
draft.remember: Midpoint: add the two x-values and halve, then add the two y-values and halve.

a.q: What is the midpoint of the interval with end points (4, 3) and (10, 9)?
a.why: x: (4 + 10) ÷ 2 = 7. y: (3 + 9) ÷ 2 = 6. So the midpoint is (7, 6). (14, 12) is wrong because it adds the values but does not divide by 2.
a.clue: Add each pair of values, then halve the total.

b.q: Mia marks the points A(−6, 2) and B(4, −8) on a map grid. What is the midpoint of AB?
b.why: x: (−6 + 4) ÷ 2 = −2 ÷ 2 = −1. y: (2 + −8) ÷ 2 = −6 ÷ 2 = −3. The midpoint is (−1, −3). (−1, 3) is tempting but drops the negative sign on the y-value.
b.clue: Take care adding a negative number to a positive one.

final.title: Midpoint of an interval
card: An interval is the part of a line between two end points. Its midpoint is the point exactly halfway between them.
To find the midpoint, average the x-values of the end points. Then average the y-values. To average two numbers, add them and divide by 2.
For end points \((x_{1}, y_{1})\) and \((x_{2}, y_{2})\), the midpoint is \(\left(\frac{x_{1} + x_{2}}{2}, \frac{y_{1} + y_{2}}{2}\right)\).
Example: the end points are \((2, 5)\) and \((8, -1)\). For \(x\): \((2 + 8) \div 2 = 5\). For \(y\): \((5 + (-1)) \div 2 = 2\). The midpoint is \((5, 2)\).
final.remember: Midpoint: add the two x-values and halve, then add the two y-values and halve.

a.q: What is the midpoint of the interval with end points \((4, 3)\) and \((10, 9)\)?
a.why: For \(x\): \((4 + 10) \div 2 = 7\). For \(y\): \((3 + 9) \div 2 = 6\). So the midpoint is \((7, 6)\). \((14, 12)\) is wrong because it adds the values but does not divide by 2.
a.clue: Add each pair of values, then halve the total.

b.q: Mia marks the points \(A(-6, 2)\) and \(B(4, -8)\) on a map grid. What is the midpoint of \(AB\)?
b.why: For \(x\): \((-6 + 4) \div 2 = -2 \div 2 = -1\). For \(y\): \((2 + (-8)) \div 2 = -6 \div 2 = -3\). The midpoint is \((-1, -3)\). \((-1, 3)\) is tempting but drops the negative sign on the y-value.
